claims.text: EF Core docs: with lazy loading, each iteration accessing a related collection triggers an additional query, its own round trip; one query for the rows plus one more per row is called the N+1 problem. Eager/explicit loading is recommended since it makes a round trip visible in the source.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/performance/efficient-querying.md, "Beware of lazy loading"

claims.text: EfOrderRepository.FindAsync uses db.Orders.Include(o => o.Items).FirstOrDefaultAsync(...); ListByCustomerAsync uses db.Orders.Where(...).Include(o => o.Customer).OrderBy(...).ToListAsync() — both eager-load their related data with one Include call each.

OrdersController.List() reads the signed-in customerId from the token, calls repository.ListByCustomerAsync(customerId), then builds the response with orders.Select(o => new OrderSummaryDto(o.Id, o.Status, o.Customer!.FullName)).ToList().

DonHangDbContext has no UseLazyLoadingProxies call or other lazy-loading configuration, so an order's Customer navigation property is never automatically populated on access; it is either eager-loaded beforehand via Include or left null.
